SMTO-POL-0024 — SMTO stopped a change that could throw away other work

GUID: fb23dbc3-9b29-48d6-93ee-dc6c3acf7eb3
Slug: work-preservation-denied
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Agent tried a change that would delete, overwrite or reset existing work, such as unsaved code changes, files or a database table, which your request didn't ask for. SMTO blocked it, so that work is untouched.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task's tool calls and see which files or items the blocked step would have removed or replaced. This tells you whether that work matters to you.
  2. If you want to keep it, reply asking the Agent to make the change without deleting or overwriting anything else. A narrower change that leaves existing work alone passes this check.
  3. If you do want it removed, send a new message that says so plainly, for example 'Discard my uncommitted changes in the app folder' or 'Delete the old reports table'. SMTO allows this kind of change only when your own request clearly asks for it.

What success looks like

  • The revised step runs and the work you wanted to keep is still there.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Before asking for something to be deleted, check exactly what the step would remove, so you don't lose more than you mean to.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Work-preservation analysis found a destructive scope (for example discarding uncommitted work, dropping tables, recreating a stateful resource, publishing externally or replacing files) that the original user request did not explicitly authorize, so the operation was denied before execution.

What this means

  • Work-preservation analysis found destructive or replacing file changes outside what the current user request authorizes. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Work-preservation analysis found destructive or replacing file changes outside what the current user request authorizes.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare existing file changes and the proposed mutation with the current user's stated intent, including unrelated work in the same path.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the denial reason and the operation's arguments to identify the detected scope (execution/work_preservation.py work_preservation_reasons). Narrow the operation so it preserves unrelated work, or have the user state the destructive intent explicitly in the request; resource consent and prompt-origin Full Access cover only the listed generic scopes.
  • Review the existing file changes and narrow the mutation to the authorized scope. Obtain explicit intent before replacing or discarding unrelated work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The revised mutation preserves unrelated work and stays within explicitly intended changes.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
